Does the validation set still look like the training set?

Source: R/checks-validation.R
feature_drift_check.Rd

Train-serve skew: a feature whose distribution has moved between X_train and X, so the model is graded on a population it was not fitted to. That is not necessarily wrong - an out-of-time holdout should differ a little - but a reviewer has to see it rather than infer it. Non-blocking: a finding routes to NEEDS_REVIEW, because a gate that hard-fails on every seasonal shift gets switched off.

Usage

feature_drift_check(config = validation_config())

Arguments

config

A validation_config(); uses drift_threshold and categorical_drift_threshold.

Value

A gate_check.

Details

Numeric features (in both frames) are compared by standardised mean shift: the difference in means over the training standard deviation, so the threshold is unitless. Anything else is compared by total variation distance between the two frequency tables, on 0-1. Missing values are dropped first, and a feature with fewer than 20 usable values in either frame, or constant in training, is not scored. One DRIFT_RISK result per drifted feature, largest shift first.

Port of FeatureDriftCheck in bdp-model-gate 0.7.0. One deliberate difference: a training column whose values are all identical is always treated as constant. Upstream tests its standard deviation against zero, which rounding defeats for values such as 0.1, and then reports shifts in the trillions.

Examples

set.seed(1)
X_train <- data.frame(age = rnorm(200, 40, 10))
X_val <- data.frame(age = rnorm(100, 46, 10))   # six years older on average
report <- run_gate(gate_context(X_val, X_train = X_train), list(feature_drift_check()))
gate_status(report)                              # NEEDS_REVIEW: drift is not blocking
#> [1] "NEEDS_REVIEW"
report$results[[1]]$detail
#> [1] "age: standardised mean shift 0.639 between training and validation (max 0.25) - the model is being graded on a different population from the one it was fitted to"
